The closeness of these estimates across different horizons indicates that I don't anticipate any dramatic shifts or accelerations in the underlying dynamics within the next month, maintaining a consistent baseline expectation.

The varying widths of the 90% confidence intervals are directly proportional to the forecasting horizon, reflecting the fundamental principle that uncertainty increases with time. While the confidence intervals aim to capture the likely range of outcomes under normal circumstances, certain significant, unforeseen events or "black swans" could push the actual results beyond these stated boundaries. For instance, sudden and and severe economic shocks, unexpected geopolitical developments, rapid shifts in relevant regulatory policies, or the emergence of disruptive technological breakthroughs could all introduce volatility far exceeding what's incorporated into the current forecast. Similarly, major and sudden changes in consumer behavior, significant supply chain disruptions, or substantial revisions in underlying data inputs could also lead to outcomes that fall outside the 90% probability range, representing rare but impactful deviations from the expected trajectory.
